blocks.text: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a haemodynamic condition characterised by an increase in mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) greater than 20 mmHg at rest, measured by right heart catheterisation (RHC).
It results from increased pulmonary vascular resistance, elevated left-sided cardiac filling pressures, increased pulmonary blood flow, or a combination of these mechanisms.
Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a specific subgroup of PH (Group 1). It is characterised by:

items.text: Pulmonary arterial wedge pressure (PAWP) 15 mmHg or less.
Pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) greater than 2 Wood units (WU).
No alternative predominant cause of pre-capillary PH, such as significant lung disease or chronic thromboembolic disease.

blocks.text: A raised pulmonary artery pressure on echocardiography alone does not establish the diagnosis. RHC is required to confirm the haemodynamic diagnosis.

items.text: Pre-capillary PH suggests a pulmonary vascular or pulmonary parenchymal process.
Post-capillary PH generally reflects elevated left atrial pressure due to left-sided heart disease.
Combined PH has both post-capillary and pulmonary vascular components.

A positive acute vasoreactivity response is defined as a reduction in mPAP of at least 10 mmHg to an absolute mPAP of 40 mmHg or less, with unchanged or increased cardiac output.

content_groups.group_title: 6.3 Group 2: PH due to left heart disease

blocks.text: The primary treatment is optimisation of the underlying cardiac condition.

items.text: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: guideline-directed heart failure therapy.
Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: control blood pressure, manage congestion and address comorbidities.
Valvular heart disease: appropriate valve intervention when indicated.
Atrial fibrillation: rate/rhythm management and anticoagulation according to standard indications.

blocks.text: PAH-specific vasodilators are not routinely recommended for PH due to left heart disease. They may worsen pulmonary congestion or cause other complications in inappropriate patients.

Definition: mPAP greater than 20 mmHg at rest on RHC.
Pre-capillary PH: mPAP greater than 20, PAWP 15 or less, PVR greater than 2 WU.
Group 4: Pulmonary artery obstruction, particularly CTEPH.
WHO FC IV: Symptoms at rest or inability to undertake physical activity without symptoms.
Initial PAH combination therapy: ERA plus PDE5 inhibitor in suitable patients.

CTEPH: Lifelong anticoagulation and assessment for pulmonary endarterectomy.

Pregnancy: PAH is associated with very high maternal risk.
Acute RV failure: Avoid excessive fluids and maintain systemic perfusion.
